author: Cptnwhizbang
body: Don't worry too much about upgrading gear past level 4 or 5 until you're 150+ at the minimum. You just level too fast to justify the material costs.

author: Maleficent_Bug_8635
body: Buffs in this game are multiplicative. If you get the shine that doubles exp, then use the exp potion that also double exp gain, you will receive 4 time the exp. So use you coins, potions and shrines, together to get through the early game.

author: [deleted]
body:
Best tip ever. 

If you don't so much moving around, get Aethric, the non-gps version of the game played on a classic RPG map. 

I started on Orna because I work for the roads department during the winter and spent a lot of time playing from the passenger seat as we drove all over the county to do our work. 

When my contract finished and I went back to working on our homestead, I realised I travel very little and even then even rarer was I in the passenger seat. So rather than sneak out at night to drive around to play, I switched to Aethric and play from the comfort of my couch. 

That being said it has about 10% of the player base so I still ask my questions on Orna :)

author: [deleted]

author: YaIe
body:
Exp is your most important resource until 10 (when you want great items, then it's back to exp). If you have to chose, don't sacrifice anything that would get you better exp.  
Run with exp boosting items. Gold, Orns and items will follow. Every 25 levels you unlock a new tier, with new mobs, new items and access to new content, the lack of Orns boosting items will be nullified by the new tiers better rewards.

author: AbsolutionVeil
body:
Your first Specialization is free, don't choose one until you get to T5. 

Early on stats are all you need to get by, but once you start raiding you'll need gear to prevent status effects.

At Lv 25 you can join a kingdom, if you can find one that's at least a Lv10 kingdom you'll have access to all the raids available in it. This is one of the best ways you'll get experience from T6 onward.

Switching Specialization loses any abilities you gained from the one you left.

author: SliceNSpice69
body: The grind is the game. Playing with combinations of gear and class/specialization is the game. There’s no endgame that isn’t grinding, so just keep that in mind. It’s not something you get past to enjoy some other type of content.
